+# The Daily Grind
+
+Static homepage with an encrypted delivery-note preview. No server or external key service is required for the preview.
+
+## Build and checks
+
+- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
+- `pnpm test`
+- `pnpm run build`
+
+The committed `assets/delivery.js` bundle is loaded directly by `index.html`. Rebuild it after changing `src/`. Serve the static files over HTTPS or localhost for Web Crypto; no build-time server entrypoint exists.
+
+## Encryption flow
+
+The default hybrid suite uses Noble's X-Wing construction, combining ML-KEM-768 and X25519. Standalone ML-KEM-768 and classical X25519 are also selectable. Bundled, pinned Noble dependencies supply the asymmetric primitives without relying on experimental native browser KEM APIs or silently downgrading protection.
+
+Each submission creates a local demonstration recipient key pair. The sender encapsulates using only its public key (or generates an ephemeral X25519 key pair in classical mode). HKDF-SHA-256 derives a non-extractable AES-256-GCM key using a random 32-byte salt and domain-separated envelope transcript hash. Encryption uses a fresh random 12-byte IV and a 128-bit authentication tag. All envelope metadata, including suite, recipient public-key fingerprint, capsule, salt, and record identifier, is authenticated. The complete header is hashed for HKDF context to remain within Web Crypto's HKDF info-length limit.
+
+Exported JSON includes only the versioned header, public capsule, salt, IV, and ciphertext with its tag. It never includes the recipient private key or plaintext. Decryption rejects modifications and suite/recipient mismatches. Plaintext is rendered through `textContent`, never as HTML.
+
+## Scope and integration
+
+This is a **local browser preview**, not an order submission flow. The UI explicitly says that notes are not sent with orders. Keys and envelopes remain in page memory. There is no localStorage, IndexedDB, analytics, or network submission of notes. Discard and replacement wipe accessible recipient secret-key byte buffers; shared-secret buffers are wiped after key derivation. JavaScript strings and managed runtime copies cannot be reliably zeroed.
+
+Reloading loses the preview key. Downloads cannot subsequently be decrypted by this page. The preview hides on tab changes and clears on page exit. Draft controls remain disabled if JavaScript fails or the browser lacks a secure Web Crypto context.
+
+Before live delivery integration, replace local recipient generation with a provisioned, authenticated delivery-service public key and key identifier. Send only encrypted envelopes to an authenticated order endpoint, bind the real order ID and recipient ID into authenticated metadata, and retain private keys only on the recipient side. Implement recipient-side decryption, authorization, key rotation, and retention there. Do not ship a delivery service private key to customers. This application-level preview is not a reviewed production end-to-end encryption protocol and does not authenticate sender identity.
+
+Photography is served from Unsplash, and typography from Google Fonts. Neither receives note contents from this implementation.

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..4580b6d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/crypto.mjs
@@ -0,0 +1,96 @@
+import { ml_kem768 } from '@noble/post-quantum/ml-kem.js';
+import { ml_kem768_x25519 } from '@noble/post-quantum/hybrid.js';
+import { x25519 } from '@noble/curves/ed25519.js';
+
+// No private key or plaintext is persisted. Production must provision an authenticated
+// delivery-service public key instead of generating the local demo recipient below.
+export const SUITES = Object.freeze({
+  hybrid: { name: 'X-Wing (ML-KEM-768 + X25519)', kem: ml_kem768_x25519 },
+  quantum: { name: 'ML-KEM-768', kem: ml_kem768 },
+  classical: { name: 'X25519', kem: null },
+});
+const encoder = new TextEncoder();
+const decoder = new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true });
+const PROTOCOL = 'daily-grind/delivery-note/v1';
+const base64 = bytes => btoa(String.fromCharCode(...bytes));
+const unbase64 = value => Uint8Array.from(atob(value), c => c.charCodeAt(0));
+const random = length => crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(length));
+
+export function createRecipient(mode) {
+  if (!Object.hasOwn(SUITES, mode)) throw new Error('Unsupported protection mode.');
+  return { mode, ...(SUITES[mode].kem ?? x25519).keygen() };
+}
+export function destroyRecipient(recipient) {
+  recipient?.secretKey.fill(0);
+}
+async function fingerprint(publicKey) {
+  return base64(new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', publicKey)));
+}
+async function deriveKey(secret, header) {
+  const material = await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', secret, 'HKDF', false, ['deriveKey']);
+  // Hash the full transcript: PQ capsules exceed Web Crypto's 1024-byte HKDF info limit.
+  const transcript = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', encoder.encode(JSON.stringify(header))));
+  return crypto.subtle.deriveKey({
+    name: 'HKDF', hash: 'SHA-256', salt: unbase64(header.salt),
+    info: encoder.encode(`${PROTOCOL}\n${base64(transcript)}`),
+  }, material, { name: 'AES-GCM', length: 256 }, false, ['encrypt', 'decrypt']);
+}
+export async function encryptNote(note, recipient) {
+  if (typeof note !== 'string' || !note.trim() || note.length > 500) {
+    throw new Error('Enter a note of 1–500 characters.');
+  }
+  const suite = SUITES[recipient.mode];
+  if (!suite) throw new Error('Unsupported protection mode.');
+  let sharedSecret, capsule;
+  try {
+    if (suite.kem) {
+      const encapsulated = suite.kem.encapsulate(recipient.publicKey);
+      sharedSecret = encapsulated.sharedSecret;
+      capsule = encapsulated.cipherText;
+    } else {
+      const ephemeral = x25519.keygen();
+      try {
+        sharedSecret = x25519.getSharedSecret(ephemeral.secretKey, recipient.publicKey);
+        capsule = ephemeral.publicKey;
+      } finally { ephemeral.secretKey.fill(0); }
+    }
+    const header = {
+      protocol: PROTOCOL, mode: recipient.mode, suite: suite.name,
+      cipher: 'AES-256-GCM', kdf: 'HKDF-SHA-256',
+      recipient: await fingerprint(recipient.publicKey),
+      id: base64(random(16)), capsule: base64(capsule),
+      salt: base64(random(32)), iv: base64(random(12)),
+    };
+    const key = await deriveKey(sharedSecret, header);
+    const plaintext = encoder.encode(note);
+    try {
+      const encrypted = await crypto.subtle.encrypt({
+        name: 'AES-GCM', iv: unbase64(header.iv), tagLength: 128,
+        additionalData: encoder.encode(JSON.stringify(header)),
+      }, key, plaintext);
+      return { ...header, ciphertext: base64(new Uint8Array(encrypted)) };
+    } finally { plaintext.fill(0); }
+  } finally { sharedSecret?.fill(0); }
+}
+export async function decryptNote(envelope, recipient) {
+  const { ciphertext, ...header } = envelope;
+  if (header.protocol !== PROTOCOL || header.mode !== recipient.mode ||
+      header.suite !== SUITES[recipient.mode]?.name || header.cipher !== 'AES-256-GCM' ||
+      header.kdf !== 'HKDF-SHA-256' || header.recipient !== await fingerprint(recipient.publicKey)) {
+    throw new Error('The envelope does not match this recipient or protection mode.');
+  }
+  const capsule = unbase64(header.capsule);
+  const suite = SUITES[recipient.mode];
+  let secret;
+  try {
+    secret = suite.kem ? suite.kem.decapsulate(capsule, recipient.secretKey)
+      : x25519.getSharedSecret(recipient.secretKey, capsule);
+    const key = await deriveKey(secret, header);
+    const plaintext = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.decrypt({
+      name: 'AES-GCM', iv: unbase64(header.iv), tagLength: 128,
+      additionalData: encoder.encode(JSON.stringify(header)),
+    }, key, unbase64(ciphertext)));
+    try { return decoder.decode(plaintext); }
+    finally { plaintext.fill(0); }
+  } finally { secret?.fill(0); }
+}

+++ b/src/delivery.mjs
@@ -0,0 +1,109 @@
+import { createRecipient, destroyRecipient, encryptNote, decryptNote, SUITES } from './crypto.mjs';
+const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
+const form = $('notes-form');
+const note = $('delivery-note');
+const fields = $('note-fields');
+const result = $('encrypted-result');
+const status = $('form-status');
+let current = null;
+let previewRevision = 0;
+const announce = (message, error = false) => {
+  status.textContent = message;
+  status.classList.toggle('error', error);
+};
+const count = () => { $('character-count').textContent = `${note.value.length} / 500`; };
+function hidePreview() {
+  previewRevision++;
+  $('decrypted-preview').textContent = '';
+  $('decrypted-preview').hidden = true;
+  $('preview-button').textContent = 'Decrypt preview';
+  $('preview-button').setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
+}
+function discard() {
+  hidePreview();
+  destroyRecipient(current?.recipient);
+  current = null;
+  $('envelope-output').textContent = '';
+  result.hidden = true;
+}
+form.addEventListener('submit', async event => {
+  event.preventDefault();
+  if (!note.value.trim()) {
+    note.setCustomValidity('Please add a delivery note before encrypting.');
+    note.reportValidity();
+    return;
+  }
+  const text = note.value;
+  const mode = new FormData(form).get('protection');
+  fields.disabled = true;
+  $('encrypt-button').textContent = 'Encrypting…';
+  announce('Encrypting your note in this browser…');
+  let recipient;
+  try {
+    recipient = createRecipient(mode);
+    const envelope = await encryptNote(text, recipient);
+    discard();
+    current = { recipient, envelope };
+    $('envelope-output').textContent = JSON.stringify(envelope, null, 2);
+    $('result-description').textContent = `${SUITES[mode].name} · AES-256-GCM · Authenticated encryption`;
+    result.hidden = false;
+    note.value = '';
+    count();
+    announce('Note encrypted. Nothing was sent. You can preview or download it below.');
+  } catch {
+    destroyRecipient(recipient);
+    announce('We couldn’t encrypt this note. Your text is still here; please try again.', true);
+  } finally {
+    fields.disabled = false;
+    $('encrypt-button').replaceChildren();
+    $('encrypt-button').append('Encrypt note →');
+  }
+});
+note.addEventListener('input', () => { note.setCustomValidity(''); count(); });
+$('clear-button').addEventListener('click', () => {
+  note.value = ''; note.setCustomValidity(''); count(); note.focus();
+  announce('Draft cleared.');
+});
+$('discard-button').addEventListener('click', () => {
+  discard(); announce('Encrypted note and preview key discarded.'); note.focus();
+});
+$('preview-button').addEventListener('click', async () => {
+  if (!current) return;
+  if (!$('decrypted-preview').hidden) { hidePreview(); return; }
+  const selected = current;
+  const revision = ++previewRevision;
+  try {
+    const plaintext = await decryptNote(selected.envelope, selected.recipient);
+    if (current !== selected || revision !== previewRevision) return;
+    $('decrypted-preview').textContent = plaintext;
+    $('decrypted-preview').hidden = false;
+    $('preview-button').textContent = 'Hide preview';
+    $('preview-button').setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
+    announce('Note decrypted and authentication verified. The preview is now visible.');
+  } catch { announce('Authentication failed. This note could not be decrypted.', true); }
+});
+$('copy-button').addEventListener('click', async () => {
+  if (!current) return;
+  try {
+    await navigator.clipboard.writeText(JSON.stringify(current.envelope, null, 2));
+    announce('Encrypted envelope copied. No private keys or plaintext included.');
+  } catch { announce('Clipboard unavailable. Use Download to save the encrypted envelope.', true); }
+});
+$('download-button').addEventListener('click', () => {
+  if (!current) return;
+  const url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([JSON.stringify(current.envelope, null, 2)], { type: 'application/json' }));
+  const link = document.createElement('a');
+  link.href = url; link.download = 'daily-grind-encrypted-note.json';
+  document.body.append(link); link.click(); link.remove();
+  setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 1000);
+  announce('Encrypted envelope downloaded. The preview key remains only in this page.');
+});
+// Do not retain revealed plaintext when leaving or switching away from the page.
+document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', () => { if (document.hidden) hidePreview(); });
+window.addEventListener('pagehide', () => { discard(); note.value = ''; count(); });
+if (globalThis.isSecureContext && globalThis.crypto?.subtle) {
+  fields.disabled = false;
+  announce('');
+} else {
+  announce('Secure notes require HTTPS or localhost and a browser with Web Crypto support.', true);
+}

+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { createRecipient, encryptNote, decryptNote, destroyRecipient } from '../src/crypto.mjs';
+const note = 'Blue door, code 8042. Please don’t ring ☕.';
+for (const mode of ['hybrid', 'quantum', 'classical']) {
+  test(`${mode}: recipient recovers Unicode note, fresh encryption, no plaintext or private key in envelope`, async () => {
+    const recipient = createRecipient(mode);
+    const a = await encryptNote(note, recipient);
+    const b = await encryptNote(note, recipient);
+    assert.equal(await decryptNote(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(a)), recipient), note);
+    for (const field of ['iv', 'capsule', 'salt', 'id', 'ciphertext']) assert.notEqual(a[field], b[field]);
+    assert.equal(atob(a.iv).length, 12);
+    assert.equal(JSON.stringify(a).includes('Blue door'), false);
+    assert.equal('secretKey' in a, false);
+    destroyRecipient(recipient);
+    assert.ok(recipient.secretKey.every(byte => byte === 0));
+  });
+  test(`${mode}: rejects tampering and wrong recipient`, async () => {
+    const recipient = createRecipient(mode);
+    const envelope = await encryptNote(note, recipient);
+    for (const field of ['ciphertext', 'capsule', 'iv', 'salt', 'id', 'recipient']) {
+      const bytes = Uint8Array.from(atob(envelope[field]), c => c.charCodeAt(0));
+      bytes[0] ^= 1;
+      const tampered = { ...envelope, [field]: btoa(String.fromCharCode(...bytes)) };
+      await assert.rejects(decryptNote(tampered, recipient), `${field} tampering must fail`);
+    }
+    await assert.rejects(decryptNote({ ...envelope, mode: 'unknown' }, recipient));
+    await assert.rejects(decryptNote({ ...envelope, cipher: 'AES-CBC' }, recipient));
+    const other = createRecipient(mode);
+    await assert.rejects(decryptNote(envelope, other));
+    destroyRecipient(other); destroyRecipient(recipient);
+  });
+}
+test('rejects unsupported modes and blank or oversized notes', async () => {
+  assert.throws(() => createRecipient('unknown'));
+  const recipient = createRecipient('hybrid');
+  for (const text of ['', '  ', 'a'.repeat(501)]) await assert.rejects(encryptNote(text, recipient));
+  destroyRecipient(recipient);
+});

+import { x25519 } from '@noble/curves/ed25519.js';
+import { ml_kem768 } from '@noble/post-quantum/ml-kem.js';
+import { ml_kem768_x25519 } from '@noble/post-quantum/hybrid.js';
+
+const utf8 = new TextEncoder();
+export const suites = {
+  classical: 'X25519',
+  hybrid: 'X25519+ML-KEM-768',
+  quantum: 'ML-KEM-768',
+};
+const base64 = bytes => btoa(String.fromCharCode(...bytes));
+const unbase64 = value => Uint8Array.from(atob(value), c => c.charCodeAt(0));
+const random = size => crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(size));
+const kemFor = mode => mode === 'hybrid' ? ml_kem768_x25519 : ml_kem768;
+
+async function deriveKey(secret, salt, header) {
+  const material = await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', secret, 'HKDF', false, ['deriveKey']);
+  const transcriptHash = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', utf8.encode(JSON.stringify(header))));
+  return crypto.subtle.deriveKey({ name: 'HKDF', hash: 'SHA-256', salt,
+    info: utf8.encode(`daily-grind/delivery-note/v1/${header.suite}/${base64(transcriptHash)}`) },
+  material, { name: 'AES-GCM', length: 256 }, false, ['encrypt', 'decrypt']);
+}
+
+export function createRecipient(mode) {
+  if (!Object.hasOwn(suites, mode)) throw new Error('Unsupported protection option.');
+  if (!globalThis.crypto?.subtle) throw new Error('Encryption requires HTTPS or localhost and a browser with Web Crypto support.');
+  const keys = mode === 'classical' ? x25519.keygen() : kemFor(mode).keygen();
+  let destroyed = false;
+  return {
+    async encrypt(note) {
+      if (destroyed) throw new Error('This session key has expired.');
+      let sharedSecret, cipherText;
+      if (mode === 'classical') {
+        const ephemeral = x25519.keygen();
+        try {
+          sharedSecret = x25519.getSharedSecret(ephemeral.secretKey, keys.publicKey);
+          cipherText = ephemeral.publicKey;
+        } finally { ephemeral.secretKey.fill(0); }
+      } else ({ sharedSecret, cipherText } = kemFor(mode).encapsulate(keys.publicKey));
+      const salt = random(32), iv = random(12);
+      const header = { version: 1, purpose: 'daily-grind/delivery-note', suite: suites[mode],
+        cipher: 'AES-256-GCM', kdf: 'HKDF-SHA-256', recipientPublicKey: base64(keys.publicKey),
+        encapsulation: base64(cipherText), salt: base64(salt), iv: base64(iv) };
+      try {
+        const key = await deriveKey(sharedSecret, salt, header);
+        const plain = utf8.encode(JSON.stringify(note));
+        try {
+          const encrypted = await crypto.subtle.encrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv,
+            additionalData: utf8.encode(JSON.stringify(header)), tagLength: 128 }, key, plain);
+          return { ...header, ciphertext: base64(new Uint8Array(encrypted)) };
+        } finally { plain.fill(0); }
+      } finally { sharedSecret.fill(0); }
+    },
+    async decrypt(envelope) {
+      if (destroyed) throw new Error('This session key has expired.');
+      const { ciphertext, ...header } = envelope;
+      if (header.version !== 1 || header.purpose !== 'daily-grind/delivery-note' ||
+        header.suite !== suites[mode] || header.cipher !== 'AES-256-GCM' ||
+        header.kdf !== 'HKDF-SHA-256' || header.recipientPublicKey !== base64(keys.publicKey)) {
+        throw new Error('Invalid encrypted note.');
+      }
+      const encapsulation = unbase64(header.encapsulation);
+      const secret = mode === 'classical' ? x25519.getSharedSecret(keys.secretKey, encapsulation)
+        : kemFor(mode).decapsulate(encapsulation, keys.secretKey);
+      try {
+        const key = await deriveKey(secret, unbase64(header.salt), header);
+        const plain = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.decrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM',
+          iv: unbase64(header.iv), additionalData: utf8.encode(JSON.stringify(header)), tagLength: 128 },
+        key, unbase64(ciphertext)));
+        try { return JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(plain)); }
+        finally { plain.fill(0); }
+      } finally { secret.fill(0); }
+    },
+    destroy() { keys.secretKey.fill(0); destroyed = true; },
+  };
+}

+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { createRecipient, suites } from './crypto.js';
+for (const mode of Object.keys(suites)) {
+  test(`${mode}: round trip, fresh randomness, and tamper rejection`, async () => {
+    const recipient = createRecipient(mode);
+    const note = { label: 'Home 🏡', note: 'Gate 2468. Quiet knock, please.' };
+    const envelope = await recipient.encrypt(note);
+    assert.deepEqual(await recipient.decrypt(envelope), note);
+    const second = await recipient.encrypt(note);
+    assert.notEqual(envelope.ciphertext, second.ciphertext);
+    assert.notEqual(envelope.iv, second.iv);
+    assert.notEqual(envelope.encapsulation, second.encapsulation);
+    assert(!JSON.stringify(envelope).includes(note.note));
+    for (const field of ['ciphertext', 'encapsulation', 'salt', 'iv', 'recipientPublicKey']) {
+      const modified = { ...envelope };
+      modified[field] = (envelope[field][0] === 'A' ? 'B' : 'A') + envelope[field].slice(1);
+      await assert.rejects(() => recipient.decrypt(modified), `${field} tampering must fail`);
+    }
+    await assert.rejects(() => recipient.decrypt({ ...envelope, suite: 'other' }));
+    await assert.rejects(() => recipient.decrypt({ ...envelope, extra: 'unauthenticated' }));
+    const other = createRecipient(mode);
+    await assert.rejects(() => other.decrypt(envelope));
+    other.destroy(); recipient.destroy();
+    await assert.rejects(() => recipient.decrypt(envelope));
+  });
+}
+test('unsupported protection fails closed', () => { assert.throws(() => createRecipient('invalid')); });

-# The DevTools Times
+# smallpt browser studio
 
-This project is a sample news application built with Astro, designed to serve as a testing ground for new features in Chrome DevTools.
+Kevin Beason’s [smallpt](https://www.kevinbeason.com/smallpt/) C++ path tracer, compiled to WebAssembly with Emscripten. The homepage is prerendered to `dist/client/index.html`. All rendering happens on the client in a module Web Worker; no rendering service is needed.
 
+## Build
 
-```sh
-pnpm install && pnpm run start
-```
+- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
+- `pnpm build` builds the Astro application using the checked-in WebAssembly artifacts.
+- `pnpm build:wasm` rebuilds `public/wasm/smallpt.js` and `smallpt.wasm` (requires `emcc`, tested with Emscripten 6.0.5).
 
-The application will now be running on `http://localhost:11224`.
+The scene renders automatically at 640 × 480 with progressive samples. Randomize changes the wall and sphere colors while preserving mirror/glass behavior. Reset restores the original palette. Quality changes restart the render, and the download control exports the displayed image as a PNG. Restarting terminates the previous worker.
 
-## Tech Stack
-
-- **[Astro](https://astro.build/)**: The web framework for building content-driven websites.
-- **[React](https://react.dev/)**: Used for UI components.
-- **[Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/)**: For styling the application.
-- **[Astro DB](https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/database/)**: Powers the comments feature, using a libSQL-compatible database.
+`renderer/smallpt-original.cpp` is the upstream source; `renderer/smallpt.cpp` preserves its path tracing integrator and replaces the CLI with a row-based browser API. Original MIT license: `renderer/LICENSE.txt`. The initial preview (`public/cornell-box.png`) is Kevin Beason’s reference render distributed with smallpt; it is replaced by live WebAssembly output as soon as the first pass completes.

+import createSmallpt from './smallpt.js';
+const renderer = createSmallpt();
+let generation = 0;
+self.onmessage = async ({ data }) => {
+  const current = ++generation;
+  try {
+    const module = await renderer;
+    if (current !== generation) return;
+    const { width, height, samples, colors, seed } = data;
+    module._initialize(width, height, seed);
+    colors.forEach((color, i) => module._set_color([0, 1, 6, 7][i], ...color));
+    const started = performance.now();
+    for (let pass = 0; pass < samples / 4; pass++) {
+      for (let row = 0; row < height; row += 8) {
+        if (current !== generation) return;
+        module._render_rows(row, 8, pass);
+        const progress = (pass * height + Math.min(row + 8, height)) / (samples / 4 * height);
+        self.postMessage({ type: 'progress', progress, elapsed: (performance.now()-started)/1000 });
+        // Yield between chunks to allow cancellation and a fresh generation.
+        await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 0));
+      }
+      const pointer = module._get_pixels();
+      const pixels = module.HEAPU8.slice(pointer, pointer + width * height * 4);
+      self.postMessage({ type: 'frame', pixels, width, height, samples: (pass+1)*4 }, [pixels.buffer]);
+    }
+    self.postMessage({ type: 'done', elapsed: (performance.now()-started)/1000 });
+  } catch (error) {
+    self.postMessage({ type: 'error', message: String(error) });
+  }
+};

+#include <math.h>   // smallpt, a Path Tracer by Kevin Beason, 2008
+#include <stdlib.h> // Make : g++ -O3 -fopenmp smallpt.cpp -o smallpt
+#include <stdio.h>  //        Remove "-fopenmp" for g++ version < 4.2
+struct Vec {        // Usage: time ./smallpt 5000 && xv image.ppm
+  double x, y, z;                  // position, also color (r,g,b)
+  Vec(double x_=0, double y_=0, double z_=0){ x=x_; y=y_; z=z_; }
+  Vec operator+(const Vec &b) const { return Vec(x+b.x,y+b.y,z+b.z); }
+  Vec operator-(const Vec &b) const { return Vec(x-b.x,y-b.y,z-b.z); }
+  Vec operator*(double b) const { return Vec(x*b,y*b,z*b); }
+  Vec mult(const Vec &b) const { return Vec(x*b.x,y*b.y,z*b.z); }
+  Vec& norm(){ return *this = *this * (1/sqrt(x*x+y*y+z*z)); }
+  double dot(const Vec &b) const { return x*b.x+y*b.y+z*b.z; } // cross:
+  Vec operator%(Vec&b){return Vec(y*b.z-z*b.y,z*b.x-x*b.z,x*b.y-y*b.x);}
+};
+struct Ray { Vec o, d; Ray(Vec o_, Vec d_) : o(o_), d(d_) {} };
+enum Refl_t { DIFF, SPEC, REFR };  // material types, used in radiance()
+struct Sphere {
+  double rad;       // radius
+  Vec p, e, c;      // position, emission, color
+  Refl_t refl;      // reflection type (DIFFuse, SPECular, REFRactive)
+  Sphere(double rad_, Vec p_, Vec e_, Vec c_, Refl_t refl_):
+    rad(rad_), p(p_), e(e_), c(c_), refl(refl_) {}
+  double intersect(const Ray &r) const { // returns distance, 0 if nohit
+    Vec op = p-r.o; // Solve t^2*d.d + 2*t*(o-p).d + (o-p).(o-p)-R^2 = 0
+    double t, eps=1e-4, b=op.dot(r.d), det=b*b-op.dot(op)+rad*rad;
+    if (det<0) return 0; else det=sqrt(det);
+    return (t=b-det)>eps ? t : ((t=b+det)>eps ? t : 0);
+  }
+};
+Sphere spheres[] = {//Scene: radius, position, emission, color, material
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec( 1e5+1,40.8,81.6), Vec(),Vec(.75,.25,.25),DIFF),//Left
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(-1e5+99,40.8,81.6),Vec(),Vec(.25,.25,.75),DIFF),//Rght
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(50,40.8, 1e5),     Vec(),Vec(.75,.75,.75),DIFF),//Back
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(50,40.8,-1e5+170), Vec(),Vec(),           DIFF),//Frnt
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(50, 1e5, 81.6),    Vec(),Vec(.75,.75,.75),DIFF),//Botm
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(50,-1e5+81.6,81.6),Vec(),Vec(.75,.75,.75),DIFF),//Top
+  Sphere(16.5,Vec(27,16.5,47),       Vec(),Vec(1,1,1)*.999, SPEC),//Mirr
+  Sphere(16.5,Vec(73,16.5,78),       Vec(),Vec(1,1,1)*.999, REFR),//Glas
+  Sphere(600, Vec(50,681.6-.27,81.6),Vec(12,12,12),  Vec(), DIFF) //Lite
+};
+inline double clamp(double x){ return x<0 ? 0 : x>1 ? 1 : x; }
+inline int toInt(double x){ return int(pow(clamp(x),1/2.2)*255+.5); }
+inline bool intersect(const Ray &r, double &t, int &id){
+  double n=sizeof(spheres)/sizeof(Sphere), d, inf=t=1e20;
+  for(int i=int(n);i--;) if((d=spheres[i].intersect(r))&&d<t){t=d;id=i;}
+  return t<inf;
+}
+Vec radiance(const Ray &r, int depth, unsigned short *Xi){
+  double t;                               // distance to intersection
+  int id=0;                               // id of intersected object
+  if (!intersect(r, t, id)) return Vec(); // if miss, return black
+  const Sphere &obj = spheres[id];        // the hit object
+  Vec x=r.o+r.d*t, n=(x-obj.p).norm(), nl=n.dot(r.d)<0?n:n*-1, f=obj.c;
+  double p = f.x>f.y && f.x>f.z ? f.x : f.y>f.z ? f.y : f.z; // max refl
+  if (++depth>5) if (erand48(Xi)<p) f=f*(1/p); else return obj.e; //R.R.
+  if (obj.refl == DIFF){                  // Ideal DIFFUSE reflection
+    double r1=2*M_PI*erand48(Xi), r2=erand48(Xi), r2s=sqrt(r2);
+    Vec w=nl, u=((fabs(w.x)>.1?Vec(0,1):Vec(1))%w).norm(), v=w%u;
+    Vec d = (u*cos(r1)*r2s + v*sin(r1)*r2s + w*sqrt(1-r2)).norm();
+    return obj.e + f.mult(radiance(Ray(x,d),depth,Xi));
+  } else if (obj.refl == SPEC)            // Ideal SPECULAR reflection
+    return obj.e + f.mult(radiance(Ray(x,r.d-n*2*n.dot(r.d)),depth,Xi));
+  Ray reflRay(x, r.d-n*2*n.dot(r.d));     // Ideal dielectric REFRACTION
+  bool into = n.dot(nl)>0;                // Ray from outside going in?
+  double nc=1, nt=1.5, nnt=into?nc/nt:nt/nc, ddn=r.d.dot(nl), cos2t;
+  if ((cos2t=1-nnt*nnt*(1-ddn*ddn))<0)    // Total internal reflection
+    return obj.e + f.mult(radiance(reflRay,depth,Xi));
+  Vec tdir = (r.d*nnt - n*((into?1:-1)*(ddn*nnt+sqrt(cos2t)))).norm();
+  double a=nt-nc, b=nt+nc, R0=a*a/(b*b), c = 1-(into?-ddn:tdir.dot(n));
+  double Re=R0+(1-R0)*c*c*c*c*c,Tr=1-Re,P=.25+.5*Re,RP=Re/P,TP=Tr/(1-P);
+  return obj.e + f.mult(depth>2 ? (erand48(Xi)<P ?   // Russian roulette
+    radiance(reflRay,depth,Xi)*RP:radiance(Ray(x,tdir),depth,Xi)*TP) :
+    radiance(reflRay,depth,Xi)*Re+radiance(Ray(x,tdir),depth,Xi)*Tr);
+}
+int main(int argc, char *argv[]){
+  int w=1024, h=768, samps = argc==2 ? atoi(argv[1])/4 : 1; // # samples
+  Ray cam(Vec(50,52,295.6), Vec(0,-0.042612,-1).norm()); // cam pos, dir
+  Vec cx=Vec(w*.5135/h), cy=(cx%cam.d).norm()*.5135, r, *c=new Vec[w*h];
+#pragma omp parallel for schedule(dynamic, 1) private(r)       // OpenMP
+  for (int y=0; y<h; y++){                       // Loop over image rows
+    fprintf(stderr,"\rRendering (%d spp) %5.2f%%",samps*4,100.*y/(h-1));
+    for (unsigned short x=0, Xi[3]={0,0,y*y*y}; x<w; x++)   // Loop cols
+      for (int sy=0, i=(h-y-1)*w+x; sy<2; sy++)     // 2x2 subpixel rows
+        for (int sx=0; sx<2; sx++, r=Vec()){        // 2x2 subpixel cols
+          for (int s=0; s<samps; s++){
+            double r1=2*erand48(Xi), dx=r1<1 ? sqrt(r1)-1: 1-sqrt(2-r1);
+            double r2=2*erand48(Xi), dy=r2<1 ? sqrt(r2)-1: 1-sqrt(2-r2);
+            Vec d = cx*( ( (sx+.5 + dx)/2 + x)/w - .5) +
+                    cy*( ( (sy+.5 + dy)/2 + y)/h - .5) + cam.d;
+            r = r + radiance(Ray(cam.o+d*140,d.norm()),0,Xi)*(1./samps);
+          } // Camera rays are pushed ^^^^^ forward to start in interior
+          c[i] = c[i] + Vec(clamp(r.x),clamp(r.y),clamp(r.z))*.25;
+        }
+  }
+  FILE *f = fopen("image.ppm", "w");         // Write image to PPM file.
+  fprintf(f, "P3\n%d %d\n%d\n", w, h, 255);
+  for (int i=0; i<w*h; i++)
+    fprintf(f,"%d %d %d ", toInt(c[i].x), toInt(c[i].y), toInt(c[i].z));
+}

+struct Vec {        // Usage: time ./smallpt 5000 && xv image.ppm
+  double x, y, z;                  // position, also color (r,g,b)
+  Vec(double x_=0, double y_=0, double z_=0){ x=x_; y=y_; z=z_; }
+  Vec operator+(const Vec &b) const { return Vec(x+b.x,y+b.y,z+b.z); }
+  Vec operator-(const Vec &b) const { return Vec(x-b.x,y-b.y,z-b.z); }
+  Vec operator*(double b) const { return Vec(x*b,y*b,z*b); }
+  Vec mult(const Vec &b) const { return Vec(x*b.x,y*b.y,z*b.z); }
+  Vec& norm(){ return *this = *this * (1/sqrt(x*x+y*y+z*z)); }
+  double dot(const Vec &b) const { return x*b.x+y*b.y+z*b.z; } // cross:
+  Vec operator%(Vec&b){return Vec(y*b.z-z*b.y,z*b.x-x*b.z,x*b.y-y*b.x);}
+};
+struct Ray { Vec o, d; Ray(Vec o_, Vec d_) : o(o_), d(d_) {} };
+enum Refl_t { DIFF, SPEC, REFR };  // material types, used in radiance()
+struct Sphere {
+  double rad;       // radius
+  Vec p, e, c;      // position, emission, color
+  Refl_t refl;      // reflection type (DIFFuse, SPECular, REFRactive)
+  Sphere(double rad_, Vec p_, Vec e_, Vec c_, Refl_t refl_):
+    rad(rad_), p(p_), e(e_), c(c_), refl(refl_) {}
+  double intersect(const Ray &r) const { // returns distance, 0 if nohit
+    Vec op = p-r.o; // Solve t^2*d.d + 2*t*(o-p).d + (o-p).(o-p)-R^2 = 0
+    double t, eps=1e-4, b=op.dot(r.d), det=b*b-op.dot(op)+rad*rad;
+    if (det<0) return 0; else det=sqrt(det);
+    return (t=b-det)>eps ? t : ((t=b+det)>eps ? t : 0);
+  }
+};
+Sphere spheres[] = {//Scene: radius, position, emission, color, material
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec( 1e5+1,40.8,81.6), Vec(),Vec(.75,.25,.25),DIFF),//Left
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(-1e5+99,40.8,81.6),Vec(),Vec(.25,.25,.75),DIFF),//Rght
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(50,40.8, 1e5),     Vec(),Vec(.75,.75,.75),DIFF),//Back
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(50,40.8,-1e5+170), Vec(),Vec(),           DIFF),//Frnt
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(50, 1e5, 81.6),    Vec(),Vec(.75,.75,.75),DIFF),//Botm
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(50,-1e5+81.6,81.6),Vec(),Vec(.75,.75,.75),DIFF),//Top
+  Sphere(16.5,Vec(27,16.5,47),       Vec(),Vec(1,1,1)*.999, SPEC),//Mirr
+  Sphere(16.5,Vec(73,16.5,78),       Vec(),Vec(1,1,1)*.999, REFR),//Glas
+  Sphere(600, Vec(50,681.6-.27,81.6),Vec(12,12,12),  Vec(), DIFF) //Lite
+};
+inline double clamp(double x){ return x<0 ? 0 : x>1 ? 1 : x; }
+inline int toInt(double x){ return int(pow(clamp(x),1/2.2)*255+.5); }
+inline bool intersect(const Ray &r, double &t, int &id){
+  double n=sizeof(spheres)/sizeof(Sphere), d, inf=t=1e20;
+  for(int i=int(n);i--;) if((d=spheres[i].intersect(r))&&d<t){t=d;id=i;}
+  return t<inf;
+}
+Vec radiance(const Ray &r, int depth, unsigned short *Xi){
+  double t;                               // distance to intersection
+  int id=0;                               // id of intersected object
+  if (!intersect(r, t, id)) return Vec(); // if miss, return black
+  const Sphere &obj = spheres[id];        // the hit object
+  Vec x=r.o+r.d*t, n=(x-obj.p).norm(), nl=n.dot(r.d)<0?n:n*-1, f=obj.c;
+  double p = f.x>f.y && f.x>f.z ? f.x : f.y>f.z ? f.y : f.z; // max refl
+  if (++depth>5) { if (erand48(Xi)<p) f=f*(1/p); else return obj.e; } //R.R.
+  if (obj.refl == DIFF){                  // Ideal DIFFUSE reflection
+    double r1=2*M_PI*erand48(Xi), r2=erand48(Xi), r2s=sqrt(r2);
+    Vec w=nl, u=((fabs(w.x)>.1?Vec(0,1):Vec(1))%w).norm(), v=w%u;
+    Vec d = (u*cos(r1)*r2s + v*sin(r1)*r2s + w*sqrt(1-r2)).norm();
+    return obj.e + f.mult(radiance(Ray(x,d),depth,Xi));
+  } else if (obj.refl == SPEC)            // Ideal SPECULAR reflection
+    return obj.e + f.mult(radiance(Ray(x,r.d-n*2*n.dot(r.d)),depth,Xi));
+  Ray reflRay(x, r.d-n*2*n.dot(r.d));     // Ideal dielectric REFRACTION
+  bool into = n.dot(nl)>0;                // Ray from outside going in?
+  double nc=1, nt=1.5, nnt=into?nc/nt:nt/nc, ddn=r.d.dot(nl), cos2t;
+  if ((cos2t=1-nnt*nnt*(1-ddn*ddn))<0)    // Total internal reflection
+    return obj.e + f.mult(radiance(reflRay,depth,Xi));
+  Vec tdir = (r.d*nnt - n*((into?1:-1)*(ddn*nnt+sqrt(cos2t)))).norm();
+  double a=nt-nc, b=nt+nc, R0=a*a/(b*b), c = 1-(into?-ddn:tdir.dot(n));
+  double Re=R0+(1-R0)*c*c*c*c*c,Tr=1-Re,P=.25+.5*Re,RP=Re/P,TP=Tr/(1-P);
+  return obj.e + f.mult(depth>2 ? (erand48(Xi)<P ?   // Russian roulette
+    radiance(reflRay,depth,Xi)*RP:radiance(Ray(x,tdir),depth,Xi)*TP) :
+    radiance(reflRay,depth,Xi)*Re+radiance(Ray(x,tdir),depth,Xi)*Tr);
+}
+
+// Keep the original integrator; expose progressive rendering to the worker.
+#include <vector>
+static int width, height;
+static unsigned int seed;
+static std::vector<Vec> accumulation;
+static std::vector<unsigned char> pixels;
+extern "C" {
+void initialize(int w, int h, unsigned int randomSeed) {
+  width=w; height=h; seed=randomSeed;
+  accumulation.assign(w*h, Vec()); pixels.assign(w*h*4, 0);
+}
+void set_color(int id, double r, double g, double b) {
+  if (id >= 0 && id < 8) spheres[id].c=Vec(r,g,b);
+}
+unsigned char* get_pixels() { return pixels.data(); }
+void render_rows(int start, int count, int pass) {
+  Ray cam(Vec(50,52,295.6), Vec(0,-0.042612,-1).norm());
+  Vec cx=Vec(width*.5135/height), cy=(cx%cam.d).norm()*.5135;
+  for(int y=start; y<start+count && y<height; ++y) {
+    unsigned short Xi[3]={(unsigned short)seed,(unsigned short)(seed>>16),
+                         (unsigned short)(y*y*y+pass*7919)};
+    for(int x=0; x<width; ++x) {
+      Vec value;
+      for(int sy=0;sy<2;++sy) for(int sx=0;sx<2;++sx) {
+        double r1=2*erand48(Xi), dx=r1<1?sqrt(r1)-1:1-sqrt(2-r1);
+        double r2=2*erand48(Xi), dy=r2<1?sqrt(r2)-1:1-sqrt(2-r2);
+        Vec d=cx*(((sx+.5+dx)/2+x)/width-.5)+
+              cy*(((sy+.5+dy)/2+y)/height-.5)+cam.d;
+        value=value+radiance(Ray(cam.o+d*140,d.norm()),0,Xi)*.25;
+      }
+      int i=(height-y-1)*width+x;
+      accumulation[i]=accumulation[i]+value;
+      Vec average=accumulation[i]*(1.0/(pass+1));
+      pixels[i*4]=toInt(average.x); pixels[i*4+1]=toInt(average.y);
+      pixels[i*4+2]=toInt(average.z); pixels[i*4+3]=255;
+    }
+  }
+}

+const canvas = document.querySelector<HTMLCanvasElement>('#render')!;
+const context = canvas.getContext('2d')!;
+const state = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#render-state')!;
+const elapsed = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#elapsed')!;
+const count = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#sample-count')!;
+const progress = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#progress')!;
+const quality = document.querySelector<HTMLSelectElement>('#quality')!;
+const frameLabel = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#frame-label')!;
+const original = [[.75,.25,.25],[.25,.25,.75],[.999,.999,.999],[.999,.999,.999]];
+let colors = original.map(color => [...color]);
+let worker: Worker | null = null;
+let hasFrame = false;
+let renderNumber = 0;
+function status(text: string) {
+  state.replaceChildren();
+  const dot = document.createElement('span');
+  dot.className = 'live-dot';
+  state.append(dot, document.createTextNode(text));
+}
+function updatePalette() {
+  colors.forEach((color, index) => {
+    const hex = '#' + color.map(value => Math.round(value * 255).toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('').toUpperCase();
+    document.querySelector(`#hex-${index}`)!.textContent = hex;
+    const swatch = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`#swatch-${index}`)!;
+    swatch.style.background = index < 2 ? hex : `radial-gradient(circle at 30% 25%, #ffffff, ${hex} 65%, #73796b)`;
+  });
+}
+function run() {
+  worker?.terminate();
+  const generation = ++renderNumber;
+  const samples = Number(quality.value);
+  progress.style.width = '0%';
+  count.textContent = `0 / ${samples} spp`;
+  elapsed.textContent = '0.0 s';
+  status('Rendering light paths');
+  try {
+    worker = new Worker('/wasm/render-worker.js', { type: 'module' });
+    worker.onerror = () => {
+      status('Renderer unavailable. Try again.');
+      worker?.terminate();
+    };
+    worker.onmessage = ({ data }) => {
+      if (generation !== renderNumber) return;
+      if (data.type === 'progress') {
+        progress.style.width = `${data.progress * 100}%`;
+        elapsed.textContent = `${data.elapsed.toFixed(1)} s`;
+      } else if (data.type === 'frame') {
+        context.putImageData(new ImageData(new Uint8ClampedArray(data.pixels), data.width, data.height), 0, 0);
+        canvas.classList.add('ready');
+        hasFrame = true;
+        count.textContent = `${data.samples} / ${samples} spp`;
+        frameLabel.textContent = 'RENDERED ON YOUR DEVICE';
+      } else if (data.type === 'done') {
+        status('Render complete');
+        elapsed.textContent = `${data.elapsed.toFixed(1)} s`;
+        progress.style.width = '100%';
+        worker?.terminate();
+        worker = null;
+      } else if (data.type === 'error') {
+        status('Render failed. Try again.');
+        console.error(data.message);
+        worker?.terminate();
+      }
+    };
+    worker.postMessage({ width: canvas.width, height: canvas.height, samples, colors, seed: crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint32Array(1))[0] });
+  } catch (error) {
+    status('WebAssembly is unavailable in this browser.');
+    console.error(error);
+  }
+}
+document.querySelector('#randomize')!.addEventListener('click', () => {
+  // Bright tints preserve the mirror and glass materials while changing their colors.
+  colors = colors.map((_, i) => {
+    const hue = Math.random() * 360;
+    const saturation = i < 2 ? .58 : .3;
+    const lightness = i < 2 ? .52 : .82;
+    const a = saturation * Math.min(lightness, 1-lightness);

+  run();
+});

+  updatePalette();
+  run();
+});

+      const result = document.getElementById('result');
+
+      button.addEventListener('click', () => {
+        button.disabled = true;
+        result.textContent = 'Loading…';
+
+        // Start critical data first, without waiting for analytics.
+        fetch('/api/data', { priority: 'high' })

+            if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}`);
+            return response.text();
+          })

+          method: 'POST',
+          headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
+          body: JSON.stringify({ click: 1 }),
+          priority: 'low',
+          keepalive: true
+        }).catch(() => {});
+      });
+    </script>

+Daily Grind registration integration
+===================================
+
+This repository is a static site. The registration interface is implemented in
+`index.html`, `rewards.css`, and `rewards.js`. It does not store accounts or pretend
+to register people locally. Deploy over HTTPS and connect the same-origin API
+below before accepting real registrations.
+
+API contract
+------------
+
+- GET /api/rewards/csrf: return JSON `{ "token": "<server-issued session-bound token>" }`.
+  Tokens must be unpredictable, cryptographically generated, 32–512 characters,
+  bound to the user's session and validated by the server on registration.
+  Use Cache-Control: no-store and a Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite session cookie.
+- POST /api/rewards/register: accept JSON with name, email, password, coffee
+  (hot/iced/both/null), updates (boolean), terms (boolean), and website (honeypot).
+  Require a valid X-CSRF-Token, same-origin Origin/Fetch-Metadata checks, and HTTPS.
+  The no-JavaScript fallback sends URL-encoded fields to the same POST endpoint;
+  either serve a server-rendered form with a server-issued hidden CSRF token or
+  reject requests without the token with an accessible error page. Never bypass
+  CSRF validation for the fallback.
+- After the server has safely accepted registration and queued a verification
+  email, return JSON `{ "status": "verification_required" }` (e.g. HTTP 202).
+  Use the same response for an existing email to prevent account enumeration.
+- Field validation: return HTTP 422 and JSON `{ "errors": { "name": "..." } }`.
+  Supported keys: name, email, password, terms. Messages must never echo passwords
+  or reveal whether an email has an existing account. HTTP 403 signals CSRF
+  failure; HTTP 429 signals rate limiting. Other/network errors remain retryable.
+
+Server responsibilities
+-----------------------
+
+Enforce all types, lengths, allowed preference values, required consent, Unicode
+names, normalized email, and password length (15–128 characters) on the server.
+Check passwords against a compromised-password blocklist. Hash passwords using
+an established password-hashing library (e.g. Argon2id); never store plaintext.
+Use parameterized database queries, uniqueness constraints and transactions to
+handle duplicate requests safely. Rate-limit registrations and verification
+emails; reject filled honeypots. Send expiring, single-use verification links.
+Do not activate accounts before verification. Record terms version and consent
+timestamps separately from optional marketing consent. Redact credentials and
+personal details from logs; never cache registration responses. No form data is
+written to localStorage, sessionStorage, URLs, or analytics by this interface.
+
+Serve the real Rewards Terms at /terms and privacy notice at /privacy-policy,
+and ensure the published program matches the advertised benefits. These routes
+and account infrastructure are not provided by this static repository.
+
+Recommended deployment headers: Content-Security-Policy (script-src 'self';
+connect-src 'self'; form-action 'self'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none';
+img-src 'self' https://images.unsplash.com; allow the existing inline stylesheet
+by its CSP hash or move it into a same-origin stylesheet), HSTS, and
+X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Restrict framing using a response header rather
+than relying on a CSP meta element.
+
+Security reference:
+https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cross-Site_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html

+# The Daily Grind INP monitoring
+
+The homepage loads the self-hosted `assets/inp-monitor.js` ES module. It uses
+`web-vitals/attribution` to measure real-user INP throughout the page lifecycle,
+including backgrounding and back/forward cache restores. No interactions means
+no INP report; unsupported Event Timing browsers do not emit a synthetic score.
+
+## Collector setup
+
+**This static repository has no analytics backend.** Provision a POST collector
+at `/analytics`, or change the `inp-endpoint` meta tag in `index.html` to your
+existing collector URL. Until that endpoint exists, reports cannot be retained.
+The collector must accept JSON encoded as a `text/plain` request body and return
+a successful response. A cross-origin collector must also permit the site's
+origin for the native `fetchLater`/fetch paths. An empty meta value disables
+collection. No credentials, collector keys, or user identifiers are required.
+
+Store/upsert records by `(id, name)`, accepting only increasing `sequence`
+values: callbacks and lifecycle sends are updates to a visit's INP, not separate
+visits. Use the latest `value`, rather than adding values or counting every
+update as a new sample. A bfcache restore gets a new metric ID from web-vitals.
+Calculate homepage p75 from the latest value for each metric ID; retain good
+visits too so slow visits do not bias the distribution.
+
+Reports include input delay, event processing duration, presentation delay,
+interaction label/type, navigation/load state, and capability flags. For values
+over 200 ms, reports also include up to five overlapping Long Animation Frames,
+with the five longest scripts in each. Counts and truncation flags identify
+omitted details. The longest intersecting script is separately included with its
+URL, function, character offset, invocation type, overlapping duration, and INP
+subpart. Use source maps from the corresponding release to resolve bundle offsets.
+
+Separate forced style/layout and rendering style/layout timings are included
+where supported. Missing timing fields are `null`, not zero. The combined
+`totalStyleAndLayoutDuration` remains available on older LoAF implementations;
+it includes both forced work inside scripts and rendering work. Aggregate totals
+cover all library-attributed frames even if frame details are truncated.
+`totalPaintDuration` is the library's estimate of off-main-thread presentation
+time, not a direct measurement of paint CPU time. Without LoAF support, INP and
+its three subparts still work, but script/rendering attribution is unavailable.
+LoAF only exposes long frames and scripts over its reporting threshold; missing
+script information does not prove that no script caused a delay.
+
+Requests use `fetchLater` when available, replacing pending snapshots as INP
+changes. The fallback sends the latest snapshot when the page becomes hidden,
+on `pagehide`, or after 60 seconds, using beacon then fetch with keepalive.
+Delivery is best effort; transport failures never block customer interactions.
+There are no unload handlers, polling loops, DOM profiling, or console logging.
+Targets are allowlisted static `data-inp-target` labels; script URL queries and
+fragments are stripped. No DOM text, form values, page queries, or account IDs
+are collected.
+
+## Build and automated checks
+
+Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm build`, and `pnpm test` after changes.
+The generated bundle and dependency license are committed so the existing static
+hosting command can serve the instrumented homepage without a build step.
+Tests exercise report attribution and transport with mocked lifecycle events;
+they do not launch a browser or server.

+# The Daily Grind
+
+The static homepage loads `assets/inp.js`, a locally bundled copy of the
+`web-vitals/attribution` INP monitor. No runtime CDN dependency is needed.
+
+Install with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, run `pnpm test`, and regenerate the
+checked-in browser asset with `pnpm build` after changing monitoring code or
+dependencies. Deploy `index.html` and `assets/` together.
+
+## Field collection
+
+The `web-vitals-endpoint` meta tag in `index.html` defaults to
+`/analytics/web-vitals`. **This repository has no backend: provision that POST
+route in your hosting/analytics infrastructure, or change the tag to your actual
+collector URL, before deployment.** A static file host alone will not store the
+reports. Set the tag's content to an empty string to disable transmission.
+
+The collector must accept JSON in a `text/plain` POST body and respond with a
+success status (for example, 204). Cross-origin collectors need suitable CORS
+headers for the fetch fallback; allow the collector in CSP `connect-src`.
+Reports use `sendBeacon`, falling back to `fetch` with `keepalive` when beacon
+queueing fails. Delivery is best effort, with no retries or local storage.
+
+Reports include all INP ratings, rather than only slow scores, so the collector
+can calculate an unbiased field distribution. Upsert by `(page, id)`, keeping the
+latest `reportedAt` report: candidate updates are snapshots of one page visit,
+not independent samples. The library also reports on page hiding and starts a
+new metric ID after a back/forward cache restore. Visits without interactions
+or browsers without Event Timing support do not produce an INP score.
+Calculate p75 across the final values for each visit, separating mobile and
+desktop using collector context. Group scores above 200 ms by target, phase,
+script URL/function/character position, and navigation type to find slow paths.
+
+## Attribution fields
+
+- `inputDelay`, `processingDuration`, `presentationDelay`: INP phase durations.
+- `interactionTarget`: stable `data-inp-target` label for each homepage link;
+  other elements use their tag name. No input values or link text are collected.
+- `longestScript`: script URL, function, character position, invoker type,
+  duration, overlapping INP duration and phase (`subpart`). Use this to locate
+  the largest observed script contributor, including third-party scripts.
+- `forcedStyleDuration` and `forcedLayoutDuration` inside `longestScript`:
+  synchronous style/layout work within that script. Older browsers can provide
+  the combined `forcedStyleAndLayoutDuration` instead.
+- `renderStyleDuration` and `renderLayoutDuration`: sums of the separate
+  rendering-phase timings across intersecting Long Animation Frames (LoAFs).
+- `totalStyleAndLayoutDuration`: library combined fallback, including both
+  end-of-frame and forced style/layout. Do not add it to the separate timings.
+- `totalScriptDuration`, `totalPaintDuration`, `totalUnattributedDuration`:
+  additional library estimates for the interaction.
+
+All durations are milliseconds. Optional timings are `null` when unavailable,
+including browsers lacking LoAF or separate style/layout timings. A measured
+zero remains zero. LoAF only attributes long frames and scripts above its
+reporting threshold; missing script attribution does not prove that no script
+caused a delay. Rendering totals describe intersecting frames, not exact
+per-phase slices, and paint is an estimate rather than a full GPU trace.
+Only the longest script is retained to keep beacon payloads small.
+
+Page and script URL query strings/fragments are omitted. Reports contain no raw
+DOM or PerformanceEntry objects. There is no console logging or visible UI.
+
+Implementation follows [Google's INP attribution guidance](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance/guides/performance/identify-inp-causes)
+and the [web-vitals library](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/web-vitals).

@@ -0,0 +1,76 @@
+# Daily Grind performance audit
+
+Audit date: 2026-11-13. Scope: the repository's single static homepage,
+its inline styles, navigation, and hero image. No browser, Lighthouse,
+development/preview server, or server entrypoint was used. No build script
+exists or is needed for this static HTML page.
+
+## Findings and changes
+
+| Area | Finding | Action / result |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| LCP discovery | Hero existed only as a CSS background, with no priority hint. | Moved it into the initial HTML as an eager `img` with `fetchpriority="high"`. The preload scanner can discover it without waiting for CSS evaluation. No duplicate preload request. |
+| Image transfer | Every screen used the same external 1350px URL. | Four same-origin, content-hashed WebP candidates with `srcset` and `sizes="100vw"`; removed the external critical-path connection. |
+| Layout stability | Hero already had a reserved height, but mobile `vh` could resize as browser chrome changes. | Retained reserved hero space, added stable `svh` with a `vh` fallback and a minimum height; image has intrinsic dimensions and fills the reserved area. |
+| Mobile interactions | Unwrapped navigation plus item margins could overflow small viewports. | Flex wrapping and gaps keep links reachable; grid columns can shrink below 250px on narrow screens. |
+| INP / main thread | No JavaScript, handlers, timers, hydration, analytics, or third-party widgets exist. | Preserved native links and zero client JavaScript. There is no source evidence of a slow handler; actual interaction latency remains unmeasured. |
+| Rendering / fonts | Small inline stylesheet, system fonts, three cards, no large DOM or expensive effects. | Kept inline CSS and system fonts. Additional CSS requests, containment, lazy-rendering machinery, or a service worker would add complexity without evidence of benefit here. |
+| Navigation | Linked routes have no implementations in this repository. | Preserved their destinations. Destination response times, backend work, and route availability require deployment context and cannot be audited from this page. |
+| Delivery | No production host, compression, or cache configuration is provided. | Recorded deployment requirements below; response headers and TTFB remain unverified. |
+
+## Measured payloads (not timing measurements)
+
+The original Unsplash URL returned **157,968 bytes** during this audit.
+`auto=format` is negotiated by the image service, so that baseline can vary
+by client and request. Local files have the following fixed sizes:
+
+| Candidate | Bytes | Difference from captured original |
+| --- | ---: | ---: |
+| 640 × 427 | 32,260 | 79.6% smaller |
+| 960 × 640 | 56,230 | 64.4% smaller |
+| 1440 × 960 | 111,724 | 29.3% smaller |
+| 1920 × 1280 | 186,470 | 18.0% larger; supplies additional large-screen detail |
+
+Only one image candidate is fetched per initial selection. Actual selection
+depends on viewport, pixel density, and browser heuristics; resizing can fetch
+another candidate. These are not mobile timing or LCP improvement claims.
+The page is **5,528 bytes raw / 1,972 bytes gzip**, with **0 bytes of client
+JavaScript** and no external runtime assets. Gzip size is computed locally;
+it does not prove the host serves compression.
+
+## Automated verification
+
+Run `npm run audit:performance` without a server or network connection.
+The check enforces HTML and per-candidate image byte budgets, validates WebP
+container lengths and encoded dimensions, verifies content hashes and srcset
+descriptors, checks fallback reuse and hero priority, and flags the introduction
+of scripts or external critical assets for performance review.
+`git diff --check` also passes.
+
+This source audit cannot establish LCP, INP, CLS, TTFB, visual rendering, or
+production cache behavior. No lab scores or field measurements are claimed.
+
+## Deployment follow-through
+
+- Serve HTML with Brotli or gzip and `Cache-Control: no-cache` so it can be
+  stored but revalidated. Avoid globally disabling caching for this public page.
+- Serve `assets/images/coffee-*.<hash>.webp` as `image/webp` with
+  `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. Regenerate the hash and
+  HTML references whenever an image changes. Publish new assets before HTML
+  and retain previous hashes through the deployment's cache lifetime.
+- Measure deployed TTFB, compression, cache headers, and all linked routes.
+  Use field data (CrUX or existing RUM) to assess the 75th percentile targets:
+  LCP ≤ 2.5 seconds, INP ≤ 200 ms, CLS ≤ 0.1, separately for mobile and desktop.
+  Runtime verification was intentionally outside this task's execution constraints.
+
+LCP approach follows [web.dev's LCP optimization guidance](https://web.dev/articles/optimize-lcp):
+make the critical image discoverable in HTML, prioritize it, and reduce its
+transfer size while assessing timing with real data.
+
+## Image provenance
+
+Preserved the existing stock photo, [Unsplash photo-1495474472287-4d71bcdd2085](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1495474472287-4d71bcdd2085).
+Each local variant was downloaded using the source URL with
+`?fm=webp&fit=crop&w=WIDTH&q=60`, where WIDTH is 640, 960, 1440, or 1920.
+The filenames contain the first 12 hexadecimal characters of each file's SHA-256.
+The photo remains decorative (`alt=""`); the heading and copy convey the hero's content.

+++ b/PERFORMANCE_AUDIT.md
@@ -0,0 +1,73 @@
+# Daily Grind performance audit
+
+## Scope and findings
+
+Audited the complete supplied site: one static HTML page with inline CSS. There
+is no application JavaScript, framework, third-party script, web font, or build
+pipeline. No server or browser was started. Runtime Core Web Vitals, network
+timings, visual image quality, and production response headers were not measured.
+
+| Area | Finding | Change |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| LCP / loading | Hero used a single external 1350px CSS background. Discovery depended on CSS parsing and loading required another origin. | Serve the same stock photograph locally as responsive WebP images, discovered directly in HTML, with eager loading and high fetch priority. |
+| Image selection | All devices requested the same image. | Provide 640, 960, 1350, and 1600px candidates. `sizes` accounts for the cover crop, the hero's 340px minimum height, and tall viewports. The browser downloads its selected candidate, not every variant. |
+| CLS / layout | Hero already reserved height, but mobile browser chrome could change its viewport-relative height. | Retain reserved space, add intrinsic image dimensions and a minimum height, and use stable viewport height where supported. The image sits outside normal flow. |
+| Mobile interactions | Navigation could overflow on narrow screens; link targets were small. | Wrap navigation, stack it below the logo on mobile, and give navigation/footer links a 44px minimum height. Mobile navigation no longer occupies sticky viewport space. |
+| Narrow screens | Grid tracks had a hard 250px minimum. | Allow tracks to shrink to the available container width. |
+| INP / main thread | No scripts, event handlers, hydration, or synchronous application tasks exist in the supplied page. No code-level slow interaction was identified. | Preserve native links and zero JavaScript. Add visible keyboard focus and respect reduced-motion preferences. |
+| Fonts / CSS | System fonts and small inline CSS already avoid extra blocking requests and font swaps. | Preserve this architecture. No library or image preload was needed; the hero is early in the HTML and has no competing asset requests. |
+
+## Measured asset sizes
+
+The original Unsplash URL returned a 157,968-byte JPEG. These are file sizes,
+not compressed HTML transfer sizes or measured load times.
+
+| Image width | Original image | Optimized WebP | Image reduction |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| 640px | 157,968 B | 32,260 B | 79.6% |
+| 960px | 157,968 B | 56,230 B | 64.4% |
+| 1350px | 157,968 B | 100,138 B | 36.6% |
+| 1600px | 157,968 B | 129,216 B | 18.2% |
+
+HTML grows from 4,708 to approximately 6,100 bytes to include responsive image
+metadata and responsive layout styles. At the same 1350px image width, combined
+HTML and image payload drops from 162,676 to approximately 106,200 bytes (35%).
+Actual image selection depends on viewport size and pixel density. Very large
+screens use the capped 1600px asset; this limits transfer size at the expense of
+some sharpness on high-density displays.
+
+## Verification
+
+- Parsed HTML with Python's standard-library HTML parser.
+- Checked that every image reference resolves to a local asset.
+- Read WebP container headers to verify actual dimensions against `srcset`.
+- Checked eager loading, high fetch priority, intrinsic dimensions, decorative
+  alternative text, and the absence of remote runtime resources or scripts.
+- Checked an HTML budget of 12 KB and a per-image budget of 140 KB.
+- Ran `git diff --check`.
+
+These checks verify the delivered code and assets. They do not establish a
+Lighthouse score or prove a Core Web Vitals improvement. No browser verification
+or dev/preview server was used, as requested.
+
+## Production follow-up
+
+Deployment configuration is not supplied, so compression, caching, TTFB, and CDN
+behavior cannot be established from this repository. Serve HTML with Brotli or
+gzip and revalidation. Cache images with an appropriate lifetime; rename assets
+when replacing them before enabling year-long immutable caching. Do not apply
+immutable caching to HTML. WebP files do not need extra compression.
+
+Evaluate production field data at the 75th percentile, separately for mobile and
+desktop: LCP <= 2.5 seconds, INP <= 200 milliseconds, and CLS <= 0.1. This is a
+validation target, not an observed result. If native-link interactions remain
+slow, inspect destination response times: the linked menu, account, order, and
+other routes have no implementations in this supplied repository and could not
+be audited here.
+
+## Image provenance
+
+Preserved the existing stock photograph from Unsplash:
+`https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1495474472287-4d71bcdd2085`.
+Downloaded explicit WebP variants using `fm=webp&fit=crop&w=<width>&q=60`.
+The page now serves these files locally and makes no request to Unsplash.
